Illness advice and information
Additionally, please note:
You can contact us using the school telephone number or email the school office.
If you are worried about your child and feel you need medical advice please call 111 for NHS advice service.The 111 service provides urgent care triage if you think you need A&E but its not life-threatening, and advice when your GP, pharmacy or dental practice is closed. If there is a danger to life or serious injury, dial 999 or go straight to A&E.

Partnerships
The Wheatley PartnershipJohn Watson School is an active member of the Wheatley Area Learning Partnership (WALP) of Schools which includes Wheatley Park School and its feeder primary schools. The partnership supports various curriculum working groups and tackles issues that affect us all. The partnership schools draw on the expertise of John Watson School for advice and support for their own pupils with special educational needs.
Oxfordshire Teaching Schools Alliance (OTSA)John Watson School is a Partner School of Oxfordshire Teaching Schools Alliance (OTSA). Teachers, support staff and governors have access to high quality training and other support including a pool of Specialist Local and National Leaders of Education. Please click on the link www.otsa.org.uk.
Comments are closed.

Transport
Transport to John Watson is managed by Oxfordshire County Council
Currently Oxfordshire County Council provides funded transport to the nearest available school for children with Special Educational Needs ( see Home to School Transport Policy below).
Parents need to complete and submit a Transport Application Form to Oxfordshire County Council.
We welcome parents who transport their own children, even on an ad hoc basis, and will provide parking outside the school on both sites. Parents may wish to park in our partner school’s carparks, to ease congestion, develop independence and community links.
Passenger Assistants (Escorts) are provided when the need has been identified through the assessment or review of the Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan.
Currently students with learning difficulties and/or disabilities (who are aged 16 to 19) will receive free travel to that placement when they attend the nearest suitable school or educational placement to their home address that has an available place.
All communication, concerns and queries regarding school transport should be directed to theOxfordshire County Council Transport team on 01865 519800

Curriculum Areas
Pupils build awareness, confidence, and independence across all areas of learning by following daily routines, developing positive interactions, and engaging in structured play, while taking pride in their progress.
Pupils develop communication, independence, and confidence through new experiences, safe risk-taking, and increasing social awareness. They are supported to build resilience, understand their roles within the community, and prepare for a successful transition to secondary education.
Pupils strengthen social communication within and beyond the classroom, developing confidence, resilience, and independence in academic and life skills. They learn to express themselves, set appropriate boundaries, and stay safe while preparing for the changes and challenges of adolescence.
Pupils prepare for adulthood by developing life skills, independence, and social understanding. They learn to engage safely and confidently with a range of people and community settings, equipping them with the resilience and skills needed for the next stage of life.
Pupils apply their skills and knowledge to real-life situations through accreditation, vocational opportunities, and community experiences. They develop self-regulation, ambition, and confidence, enabling them to pursue their interests, function well in society, and move forward from John Watson School fully prepared for adulthood.
Class sizes are typically small, with around 8–10 pupils supported by a class teacher and three teaching assistants, although this may vary depending on the needs of the group. Pupils are grouped broadly by chronological age, but we also take into account their individual needs, learning profiles and preferred approaches to learning to ensure the best possible fit. Each key stage has its own focus, reflecting the developmental priorities and curriculum intent for that age group, while maintaining clear continuity and shared principles across the school. Parent’s/Carer’s Right to Withdraw from RSE
Q: Do I have a right to withdraw my child from Relationships and Sex Education?
A: Parents will continue to have a right to request to withdraw their child from sex education delivered as part of RSE in secondary schools which, unless there are exceptional circumstances, should be granted up to three terms before their child turns 16. At this point, if the child themselves wishes to receive sex education rather than be withdrawn, the school should make arrangements for this to happen in one of the three terms before the child turns 16 – the legal age of sexual consent.
There is no right to withdraw from Relationships Education at primary or secondary as we believe the contents of these subjects – such as family, friendship, safety (including online safety) – are important for all children to be taught.For more informarion, please see: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/relationships-education-relationships-and-sex-education-rse-and-health-education-faqs
Comments are closed.

Meet the Governors
Chris is the Vicar of St Barnabas Jericho and St Thomas the Martyr, Oxford; and is delighted to serve as Chair of Governors at John Watson School. Chris is a Governor of St Barnabas Church of England Primary School in Jericho, where he used to serve as Vice-Chair and the Chair. Chris is passionate about helping every child flourish, and is especially committed to inclusive education, strong pastoral care and working closely with staff, families and the wider community. Originally from Northern Ireland he has lived in England since 2007 and worked in Cambridge and London before moving to Oxford in 2019.
Liz is an early years consultant who has a long history of supporting quality in the early years. Liz worked for Ofsted for fourteen years, in various roles including inspection framework development, training inspectors and latterly as head of early years policy. Since taking early retirement in 2013 Liz has worked as a consultant on various early years projects in England and internationally. She has a keen interest in building links in the local community and is currently a governor at Wheatley Primary School and a trustee of the Maple Tree children’s centre.
Clea is the Wellbeing Governor
Clea has had a long connection with the school, with over 13 years teaching experience across the age range and has been on the governing body since 2015 as a co-opted governor. Clea is a part time teacher at the school, based on the primary site, with a particular interest in family and community engagement.
Sam joined the governing body as a parent governor in October 2021. Samuel is a qualified accountant with more than 20 years working experience. He has always been passionate about making a difference in people’s lives, joining Leo’s and Lions International in his teens and volunteering with Rotary international for a short while.
Samuel grew up in South Africa and, prior to moving to the UK 7 years ago, worked for TAFTA (The Association For The Aged) as Divisional Manager of Finance and Divisional Manager of Admin and Income Development. Samuel also holds a fractional appointment with the University of KwaZulu-Natal, where he works as the Director of Operations for the Health Economics and HIV/Aids Research Division, working on strategic projects and partnerships and overseeing the finance department.
In the UK, Samuel is employed as finance manager of two companies based in Oxford. He previously served on a school board in South Africa at the Browns School and also served as a board member for the African Capacity Alliance based in Nairobi, Kenya.
James joined the governing body as a parent governor in October 2021. James has had a career as a researcher, consultant and project manager, focusing on agriculture in Africa, and China and international development. After graduating, he spent four years as a VSO language teacher in China, before returning to the UK to undertake postgraduate study, and then to work as a researcher at the Institute of Development Studies, University of Sussex. He recently relocated to the UK with his family after ten years in Ethiopia and China, where he managed a collaboration between the UK and Chinese governments supporting agricultural development in Africa. He was previously a Senior Researcher at the International Institute for Environment and Development. He speaks Mandarin.
Lois joined John Watson School in September 2018 and is an Assistant Headteacher and a Key Stage 1 teacher. Lois completed a degree in Psychology in Barbados and, during this time, volunteered at a special school. She moved to the UK in 2016 and has worked in schools in Oxford.
Sara was elected as a parent governor in October 2024.She has been a Consultant Plastic Surgeon at the Oxford University HospitalsNHS Trust since 2014. She has significant experience in trauma and children’sreconstructive surgery, both from time in Oxford, Yorkshire and internationally.She has more recently co-founded a scar and laser skin company situated inWheatley.Sara’s roles have ranged from governance, to leadership and operationalmanagement. She is an examiner for the Royal College of Surgeons helpingmaintain standards for future surgeons and is currently the lead for PlasticSurgery Trauma at the Oxford Major Trauma Centre at the John Radcliffe.Many of the skills and experience from her surgical work and her passion forimproving complex health systems are translatable to the school setting.
Jemima is a Partnerships Coordinator and Teacher of English at Magdalen College School and developed a relationship with John Watson in 2021 when she delivered drama workshops at the primary school. Jemima completed a degree in English and Education Studies at Durham University and went on to complete a Diploma in Education at Northumbria University. She taught Maths in Stockton-on-Tees for two years before moving to Oxford in 2020 to work at Magdalen College School.
Jemima is particularly passionate about sustainability and environmental education, as well as broadening access to drama and the arts.
